source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ παρὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἄζυμα λαμβάνειν, ἢ κοινωνεῖν ταῖς ἀσεβείαις αὐτῶν.
thought_title: No unleavened bread or fellowship with Jewish impiety
orientation: The council continues its rulings against sharing in Jewish religious practices, now forbidding Christians to take unleavened bread from Jews or to share in their impiety.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not right to take unleavened bread from the Jews, or to share in their impieties.

choices.why: The standard English term for the Jewish Passover bread, preserving the concrete object the canon forbids receiving.
The verb κοινωνεῖν takes a dative of the thing shared in; 'share in' preserves the participative sense without implying Eucharistic communion, which the glossary reserves for κοινωνία.
rejected: to have communion with their impieties

choices.why: The plural abstract noun denotes acts or practices of impiety, matching the source's plural and avoiding the more general 'ungodliness.'

pass_b_english: It is not right to take unleavened bread from the Jews, or to share in their impieties.
